purpose: Functional and visual parity tests. A boot/idle smoke pass never implies mission or attack correctness.

controls.standalone_default: Modern controls enabled unless SPIDEY_MODERN_CONTROLS=0. Mouse buttons map through existing action bindings.

evidence_required: Exact binary hash and source commit.
Map, difficulty, challenge variant and all explicit SPIDEY_* settings.
Input script timed by game ticks, initial camera/player/actor state and every test-only mutation.
GDB crash stack and process exit status.
Before/after screenshots plus post-clip vertex/region diagnostics.
Animation ID/frame, actor state/health, effects allocation/retirement, audio sample and decoder status.

setup: Clear inherited SPIDEY_* settings; keep only explicit scenario settings.
Start from title with movies enabled and audio output available.
steps: Let each logo and the first mission movie finish naturally.
Enter New Game, choose Normal, let Black Cat scene finish.
checks: Decoded movie frames reach their declared final frame.
Video and audio advance together; output includes nonzero PCM samples.
Gameplay begins with no remaining movie decoder.
reference: Original Wine game with the same menu input schedule.

setup: Run once in Normal and once in Kid mode.
steps: Press Escape during each FMV after its first decoded frame.
Press Escape during an eligible in-engine scene.
Press Escape again during gameplay, then resume.
checks: FMV decoder exits and its audio stops.
Eligible scene actors/camera clean up; player control resumes.
Gameplay Escape opens the pause flow without firing an attack.
Unskippable scenes follow the original rules.
reference: Original cutscene eligibility flags and cleanup function disassembly.

setup: Start New Game without skipping the Black Cat conversation.
Enable SPIDEY_TRACE_PLAYER, SPIDEY_TRACE_ANIMS and SPIDEY_TRACE_BADDY.
steps: Record player and Black Cat animation ID/frame at every game tick.
Capture matched camera frames at dialogue start, middle and end.
checks: Animation ID/frame and transition sequence agree with the oracle at the same tick.
Hands stay attached to the correct joints and do not reflect across the character.
Black Cat approaches and faces the player correctly.
Every spoken clip produces audio and retires on completion.
reference: ~/Documents/spidey-work/oracle/oracle.py
~/Documents/spidey-work/refcap.sh

setup: Set SPIDEY_FULL_MAP=1 and SPIDEY_TRACE_CULL=1.
Keep camera position and yaw in every capture.
steps: Turn through 360 degrees on the spawn roof.
Move across the first two connected sections.
Look toward the far skyline at minimum and maximum camera distance.
Repeat after a restart.
checks: Every referenced environment model region is usable.
Full-map distance culling does not remove buildings.
Nearby geometry remains visible when the camera passes its bounding sphere.
No missing model, invalid region, nonfinite vertex or extreme post-clip triangle is submitted.
reference: Original Wine frames from the same camera/input script.
Original model/region tables; standalone-only full-map policy is an intentional difference.

setup: Use default modern controls and record sensitivity.
steps: Move mouse left/right through two full turns.
Move mouse up/down to each pitch limit.
Move forward/backward while repeating the sweep.
Alt-tab out and back, then resume.
checks: Camera yaw has the requested direction and speed.
Horizon does not acquire roll during horizontal movement.
Camera matrix stays finite and the player remains attached to the map.
UI/cinematics do not receive gameplay mouse-look input.
Focus changes release held inputs and restore control.
reference: Original camera math disassembly; modern input policy is intentional.

setup: Record BaddyList and control/script actors separately.
Identify each object by class/type, node, region/model and spawn tick.
steps: Traverse every enemy spawn trigger on the route to the exit.
Wait for each group to activate.
Backtrack, restart the area and repeat.
checks: Spawn class, count, node and position match the original at each trigger.
Enemies use valid model regions, joints and textures from their first visible frame.
Live enemies enter their expected AI states and contact the floor.
Script-only actors remain on their control list.
Dead enemies release handles, AI procedures and protected effects.
reference: Original Wine process state sampled by a parent-launched oracle at the same trigger/tick.

setup: Approach an unmodified live enemy through real player input.
steps: Observe the enemy before attacking.
Punch with left mouse, kick with its mapped action, then alternate a full combo.
Circle the enemy with mouse-look while it attacks.
Defeat it and wait for cleanup.
checks: Enemy renders before the first hit, throughout hit/fall states and until its original death transition.
Health changes and AI reactions agree with original hit data.
No body part forms a triangle extending toward the window corner.
No invalid animation/part, script error or crash occurs.
SFX voices return to their idle pool.
reference: Original hit/AI functions and Wine combat captures.

setup: Select the web-ball attack using W plus right mouse in the current default mapping; record signed analogue bytes.
Use an unchanged live enemy; any player teleport for deterministic setup must be recorded.
steps: Fire from a clear line of sight.
Repeat at close, medium and long range.
Fire while strafing and while turning the camera.
checks: CImpactWeb is allocated at the shot frame.
Scale rises from zero and position advances using elapsed game ticks.
The sprite and impact ring are visibly submitted.
The swept collision calls the target Hit with original damage/direction data.
Projectile, crater/ring and child web fragments expire without leaks.
reference: Original CImpactWeb::Move at 0x4F9BD0 and its supporting vtables.

setup: Aim away from live actors, then toward a solid wall.
steps: Fire into open air until its lifetime expires.
Fire into a wall with a precomputed environment hit.
Fire at a web-operable switch where available.
checks: Open-air projectile advances and expires with no fake target damage.
Wall impact uses its hit position/normal and draws a fading crater.
Switch activates once if original face flags allow it.
No projectile remains invisible at age zero.
reference: Original constructor/Move, CSplat and CSwitch behavior.

setup: Stand within range of an unchanged live enemy.
Record any deterministic player teleport and initial actor state.
steps: Hold S plus right mouse until the normal FireWeb selects a target.
Reach each release animation threshold, then let the loose web finish.
Repeat from either side and at different height offsets.
checks: No native jump to original Windows code occurs.
Accepted tug changes mode 1 to 2 and creates a valid CChain.
Target receives TugImpulse and expected damage/AI change.
Player active web pointer clears after release.
Line and chain retire; attached handles are not reused after deletion.
reference: Original CWeb::SwitchToSnap 0x4F69F0 and original-machine-code differential fixtures.

setup: Find a non-tuggable type50 actor and a manip object type401.
Keep original callback accept/reject behavior.
steps: Tug an accepted manip object.
Tug a rejected target.
Repeat with a target removed before the release frame.
checks: Type401 uses its two-vector impulse callback; ordinary actors use the three-argument virtual.
Rejected tug creates loose fragments and dies.
Null recovered target still creates the original loose chain.
Fragments update both endpoints, ground damping, extra segments and signed age expiry.
reference: Original BreakIntoBits, fragment constructor/Move, Mem_RecoverPointer.

setup: Begin on a roof with valid swing and zip anchor surfaces.
steps: Jump and start a swing, hold for two arcs, release and land.
Zip to a wall, climb, transition to ceiling and back.
Interrupt a swing with a permitted attack.
checks: A visible web joins the hook/anchor and follows both endpoints.
Animation/state transitions and attachment hooks agree with original.
Released web retracts or fragments and expires.
Movement and collision remain valid at map boundaries.
reference: Original CPlayer/CSwinger functions and matched Wine key script.

setup: Record trigger IDs and links as u16 words from the original level data.
steps: Collect each nearby pickup/tutorial entry.
Move onto the next building or section immediately afterward.
Revisit the trigger and repeat after restart.
checks: Pickup effect, resource/health change, tutorial and speech occur once as originally required.
Links point at valid nodes; no Bad node sent to Trig_GetLinksPointer error.
Level exit/load preserves player/camera/audio state.
reference: Original trigger/script functions and Wine route capture.

setup: Use audible output, then repeat with dummy output for sample assertions.
steps: Play ordinary effects and non-default pitch effects.
Generate more than 124 sequential short effects.
Start/stop a loop; pause/resume and change the level.
checks: Frequency zero restores each buffer sample rate.
All 256 pitch bytes preserve original conversion and DXSOUND argument order.
Short effects finish, loops remain live until stopped, and voices are reclaimed.
Volume/pan remain finite and effects are neither slowed to 100 Hz nor clipped by overflow.
reference: Original playSFX/DXSOUND_SetPitch disassembly and real SDL callback fixture.

setup: Keep FMV, music/dialogue and SFX lifetimes separate.
steps: Let music play during movement/combat.
Trigger two dialogue lines and wait for completion.
Pause/resume, stop/restart and change the level during playback.
Skip a cinematic while a sound is active.
checks: Stream contains decoded nonzero audio samples.
Original completion/status and pause behavior advance scripts correctly.
Bounded decode does not accumulate whole long tracks in memory.
All decoder children and audio queues retire at stop, EOF and shutdown.
reference: Original PCMUSIC/ADXT calls and real Bink assets.

setup: Start from a fresh area state using its original difficulty and entrance.
steps: Complete all area objectives and required enemy groups.
Activate the exit with real gameplay input.
Load the next area, then exercise death/retry/checkpoint.
checks: Objectives, boss phases, scripted waves, hostages and exit requirements match original.
Next map loads usable regions and correct actor lists.
Checkpoint/save/retry restore the intended area and resources.
reference: Original full mission route recorded under Wine.

setup: Record GL renderer, resolution, MSAA and texture filtering settings.
steps: Capture fixed-position views with quality setting disabled and enabled.
Move camera past oblique roofs/walls and repeating textures.
Inspect HUD text, sprites, atlas edges and transparent effects.
checks: Quality setting changes only supported world sampling.
No adjacent atlas tiles bleed into HUD/sprite textures.
No unsupported GL enum or incomplete texture is created.
Temporal shimmer improvement is measured before it is claimed.
reference: Original point/bilinear filter policy; optional standalone quality change measured independently.

setup: Load the specified challenge variant, rather than only its shared base map.
steps: Perform the requested actions until success.
Miss an objective, restart, and repeat.
checks: Challenge counter, timer and success/failure behavior agree with original.
Correct target/enemy model and animation render throughout.
Restart clears transient effects, audio and scores.
reference: Original training table, scripts and Wine challenge completion.

setup: Use an unchanged enemy and normal difficulty. Record player health, level status, menu state and timer ticks.
steps: Enter active combat and allow a real enemy to defeat Spider-Man.
Let the Game Over menu render. Wait for at least 30 advancing menu frames.
Press Enter on Retry. Observe the selected result and wait for the map to reload and regain player control.
Repeat death on a fresh run. Press Down then Enter on Quit and observe return to the expected shell/menu.
checks: Menu timer and selection advance; a paused stack snapshot alone does not prove a hang.
Retry and Quit return their original distinct results.
Retry reloads objects and audio without stale pointers or a crash.
The new player is unlocked and has the original starting health.
reference: Original Front_ContinueExit and Pause disassembly. Original Wine menu selection and map reload.

setup: Capture the exact camera matrices and sprite world positions. Run once with fixed camera and once during a left/right and up/down mouse sweep.
steps: Fire a web ball at a nearby enemy, at a distant wall and into clear space.
Record each projectile Move, draw submission, impact ring/fragment allocation and retirement.
Repeat with ordinary webs, damage effects and pickups, at several positive camera depths and behind the camera.
checks: Projected depth uses the transformed third row and the original projection distance.
Homogeneous world position has W=1 and the active camera matrix is refreshed before projection.
Visible sprites submit finite quads overlapping the viewport with valid texture handles and positive reciprocal depth.
Sprites behind the camera obey the original clip rules.
Effects neither stretch to a window corner nor use stale depth after camera rotation.
reference: Original gte_rtps 0x46DBC0 and DisplayFlatBitList 0x40DBD0 disassembly, plus matching Wine frames.
